captures.q: What are the arguments in “Monetary Substrate Audit 001 — Productive Operator Transport: Sappho–Carson as a Test Vector for Monetary Translation (EA-MSAL-0001 v0.2, provisional)” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE AUDIT READ AS AN AUDIT, ITS NUMBER REJECTED AS THE AUDIT REJECTS IT: asked for the arguments of Monetary Substrate Audit 001, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1620 from the archive (Alexanarch) as the paper sets itself out: the commensuration contract (§4) and the transformed relations (§8); the suspended distinctions, quoted ('For the scalar to operate, it only has to cease requiring them.'), in a section it titles 'What the Scalar Does Not Require' (the paper's §6 is 'Suspended distinctions'); the settlement-disqualified distinctions (§7); selection pressure (§13), with the paper's own example (unseen uptake 40 to 15) and its chain 'qualitative distinction → parameter → operative standing'; the working figure $35.1 million in $13.7M–$86.5M, from $503.7 trillion and a one-part-per-million incidence; six of the seven defects (the 588-observation denominator, the unsupported 40, the population mismatch, the units that do not close, the incidence, the proxy), the repairable kept apart from the unrepairable; the verdict 'witness / unsound' with the auditor's relation noted; and 'the semantic account therefore remains open' placed before §17.

atoms.evidence: The article by Lee Sharks, Monetary Substrate Audit 001
Monetary Substrate Audit 001 — Productive Operator Transport: Sappho–Carson as a Test Vector for Monetary Translation
A hypothetical option-value estimate for productive operator transport, not the value of Sappho, Carson, or their poetry.
It builds a numerical model and then audits that model.
is an examination of what happens when a literary and interpretive phenomenon is translated into a monetary valuation
That relationship weakens the audit rather than automatically invalidating it.
